title: Key:piste:difficulty
notes: Read via WebFetch this session (two passes, one asking generally, one asking specifically about the piste:type=downhill section). This is OSM's own documentation for the exact tag (piste:difficulty on piste:type=downhill ways) this project's step 03 compares against DEM-derived slope (C052). It gives no numeric slope-percent or slope-degree threshold for the downhill/alpine difficulty values (novice/easy/intermediate/advanced/expert/freeride) -- only regionally-varying colour/shape schemes. It does give a numeric inclination table, but only for a different piste type, piste:type=ski_touring, attributed to the Swiss Alpine Club (SAC) ski-touring grading scale.

title: The Ski Safety Act, Colorado Revised Statutes Title 33, Article 44
notes: PDF fetched via WebFetch this session (WebFetch's own summarization could not reliably read the compressed PDF text, so the binary it saved was re-read directly with pypdf in this session to quote-verify). Cover/footer reads "SKI SAFETY ACT ... Effective July 1, 2006". Section 33-44-103(3.1) defines "Extreme terrain" numerically: "any place within the ski area boundary that contains cliffs with a minimum twenty-foot rise over a fifteen-foot run, and slopes with a minimum fifty-degree average pitch over a one-hundred-foot run." Section 33-44-107(2)(a)-(c) defines the green-circle/blue-square/black-diamond trail-marking symbols purely descriptively ("least difficult", "most difficult", "falls between"), with no numeric slope threshold for any of the three. This is Colorado state law, not a BC/Canadian standard and not specific to RMR.
